rows.subtype: Family adjusting to a shift worker [Receiver]
rows.description: Family of a shift worker may feel neglected as meals and events are missed, while the worker feels guilty and worn out. Planning shared time, keeping the house quiet for sleeping and open talk hold the relationship together.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22

rows.subtype: Business traveller and a tired mind [Observer]
rows.description: A colleague sees someone after a long trip making poor judgments, being unusually irritable or dozing in meetings. Allowing a day to adjust and not scheduling crucial decisions right away is fair and practical.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22

rows.subtype: Adapting wisely to a disrupted clock [Response]
rows.description: A person guards a fixed sleep window, uses light and darkness on purpose, eats sensibly and avoids important decisions when sleep-deprived. If exhaustion or low mood persists, they discuss it with a doctor.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22

rows.subtype: Toddler recharging after a big day [Actor]
rows.description: A toddler after an outing wants quiet, a familiar toy and closeness, and may fall apart if pushed to do more. Rest is part of how small children absorb what they have experienced.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young child who learns to spend a short time with books, drawing or gentle music discovers that calm can be restful, not boring. Adults who value quiet time show that rest is not laziness.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A schoolchild after a long day of noise and effort may be irritable or silent and need time alone before homework and talking. Snacks and unstructured play often work better than immediate questions.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Teen packed with classes and coaching [Actor]
rows.description: A teenager in a schedule of school, tuition and activities has no space to rest and feels flat, resentful or anxious. Building free time into the week is not wasted, since the mind consolidates and recovers in it.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult who feels lazy whenever not productive finds rest empty and anxious. Learning that recovery makes later work better allows genuine rest without guilt.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A person notices what really refreshes them, such as a walk, a hobby, time with friends or plain quiet, rather than scrolling. They protect it in the week and treat it as maintenance, not a reward.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtype: Colleague or partner respecting a need for rest [Observer]
rows.description: A partner or coworker sees someone depleted and does not push for more, offering space and practical relief instead. Being allowed to recover, without guilt or judgment, strengthens the relationship.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: admiration, guilt, relief
